page: Google Cloud Platform c4-standard-96-lssd is a high-performance server instance powered by an Intel Xeon 6985P-C processor built on the x86_64 architecture. It features 96 dedicated virtual CPUs, which correspond to 48 physical cores with hyper-threading, operating at a base frequency of 2.3 GHz. The processor is supported by a substantial 504 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 360 GB of system memory, providing 3.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. Storage is a key highlight, featuring 6167 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity distributed across 16 local drives, while no dedicated GPU hardware is included.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier performance across several compute and memory sub-systems. The processor's advanced instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, contribute to strong multi-core performance, as evidenced by a Passmark CPU score of 110,513.48 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 20,352.0. Memory subsystem throughput is exceptionally high, with read-only cached small block bandwidth reaching 7,717.61 GB/sec and uncached large block read bandwidth at 356.38 GB/sec. Additionally, the platform demonstrates strong capabilities in data processing, achieving 171.76 million Redis SET operations per second and a static web serving throughput of 150.43 GB/sec.

Given the combination of high-density local NVMe storage, high memory bandwidth, and advanced CPU instruction sets, this instance is highly optimized for storage-intensive and database workloads. It is well-suited for high-throughput database operations, software compilation, and large-scale data decompression tasks. While it lacks a dedicated GPU, the integrated Intel AMX capabilities enable strong performance for CPU-based machine learning tasks, such as prompt processing for medium-sized LLMs. The primary tradeoff is the relatively moderate memory-to-vCPU ratio of 3.75 GB per core, which may limit workloads requiring massive in-memory datasets without active storage paging.
